extracted_claims.text: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 entered into force on 1 August 2024 and Article 113 originally set the general date of application as 2 August 2026.
Under the originally adopted AI Act, the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III were scheduled to apply from 2 August 2026.
The European Parliament's official summary states that high-risk system obligations become applicable 36 months after entry into force (i.e., around August 2027), rather than 24 months (August 2026).

In November 2025, the European Commission proposed (COM(2025)836, the 'Digital Omnibus on AI') to delay application of the Chapter III, Sections 1-3 high-risk obligations, citing delayed availability of standards, common specifications and national competent authorities, and proposed shifting application by up to 16 months or tying it to confirmation that needed standards/tools are available.
On 7 May 2026, the Council and European Parliament reached political agreement to adjust and simplify the timeline for high-risk AI system rules under the Digital Omnibus proposal.

The consolidated text of Regulation 2024/1689 as amended (version dated 27 July 2026, reflecting the adopted Digital Omnibus on AI) ties the application of high-risk obligations to 'the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113', rather than fixing 2 August 2026.
Per the EU AI Act Service Desk (current guidance), the rules for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III will now enter into application on 2 December 2027.

Obligations for high-risk AI systems that are classified as high-risk because they are safety components/products under existing EU harmonisation legislation (Annex I) will enter into application on 2 August 2028.

A legal-analysis source states that obligations on Annex I-type (non-Annex III) high-risk AI systems used as safety components apply 36 months after entry into force (i.e., around August 2027), rather than August 2028.

Some commentary (dated prior to final adoption) asserts that 2 August 2026 remains the binding/operative enforcement date for Annex III high-risk obligations because the proposed delay 'has not been enacted into law.'
Other commentary states that Annex III high-risk obligations 'became enforceable on August 2, 2026,' without reference to any later delay.
The Digital Omnibus on AI is described as having 'entered into force on 27 July 2026,' which is the legal basis for moving the Annex III application date to 2 December 2027.

Article 111(2) of the Regulation (as amended) provides that for high-risk AI systems placed on the market or put into service before the date of application of Chapter III (Article 113), the Regulation applies to their operators only if those systems undergo significant design changes after that date; providers/deployers of high-risk systems intended for use by public authorities must still take necessary steps.

Other EU AI Act provisions have different application dates: prohibited practices (Chapter I-II) applied from 2 February 2025; GPAI rules, governance (Chapter III Section 4, Chapter V, VII, XII, Art. 78) applied from 2 August 2025; and general application (including transparency obligations under Article 50) applies from 2 August 2026, with a further transition to 2 December 2026 for Article 50(2) marking/detection obligations for systems already on the market.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI System Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III, following entry into force on 1 August 2024 ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025PC0836), [AZComply](https://www.azcomply.eu/en/learn/ai-act-fundamentals/6)) (high confidence). However, following a Commission proposal in November 2025 (the "Digital Omnibus on AI") and a political agreement between Council and Parliament on 7 May 2026, this date has been pushed back to **2 December 2027**, as now reflected in the amended consolidated Regulation text and the EU AI Act Service Desk's current guidance ([EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation)) (high confidence). Some sources not reflecting this amendment still cite 2 August 2026, which should be treated as outdated.

## Key Findings

### Original Legal Timeline
Regulation 2024/1689 entered into force on 1 August 2024, with Article 113 originally setting the general application date at 2 August 2026, including obligations for Annex III high-risk systems ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025PC0836), [Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline)) (high confidence). This 2 August 2026 date for Annex III obligations specifically is corroborated by multiple sources, though with lower individual source authority (low confidence) ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20)).

### The Digital Omnibus Amendment
In November 2025, the European Commission proposed delaying Chapter III Sections 1–3 high-risk obligations, citing delays in the availability of harmonised standards, common specifications, and national competent authorities (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025PC0836), [Consilium](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). On 7 May 2026, Council and Parliament reached political agreement to adjust and simplify this timeline (medium confidence) ([Consilium](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). The consolidated Regulation text dated 27 July 2026 now ties high-risk obligations to "the date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113" rather than fixing 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727)).

### Current Applicable Date: 2 December 2027
Per the EU AI Act Service Desk's current guidance, Annex III high-risk AI system rules will now enter into application on **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)). Separately, obligations for high-risk systems classified as such because they are safety components under existing EU harmonisation legislation (Annex I) will apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)).

### Transitional Rules
Article 111(2) of the amended Regulation provides that for high-risk systems placed on the market before the Chapter III application date, the Regulation applies to operators only if the systems undergo significant design changes afterward; providers/deployers for public authorities must still take necessary compliance steps (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

### Other Application Dates (Context)
Prohibited practices applied from 2 February 2025; GPAI rules and governance provisions applied from 2 August 2025; general application (including Article 50 transparency obligations) applies from 2 August 2026, with a further transition to 2 December 2026 for marking/detection obligations under Article 50(2) (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Several sources state the Annex III deadline remains 2 August 2026, treating the delay as an unenacted proposal (low confidence) ([Cloud Security Alliance](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-high-risk-compliance-deadline-20), [Belgrave Whitmore](https://www.belgravewhitmore.com/guides/eu-ai-act-high-risk-systems)); these appear outdated relative to the amended consolidated text and official Service Desk guidance. The European Parliament's topic page cites a 36-month timeline (~August 2027) for high-risk obligations, conflicting with the originally adopted 24-month (August 2026) date cited elsewhere (medium confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)). Similarly, one legal-analysis source states Annex I obligations apply 36 months after entry into force (~August 2027), a full year earlier than the 2 August 2028 date cited by most other sources (low-to-medium confidence) ([artificialintelligenceact.eu](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/ai-act-implementation-next-steps)).

## Knowledge Gaps
It remains unclear whether the Digital Omnibus amendment has been formally published in the Official Journal as a finalized legislative act, as distinct from a consolidated working text or political agreement. The precise conditions under which the 2 December 2027 date could shift further (e.g., tied to confirmed availability of harmonised standards) are not fully specified in available sources. The interaction between Article 111's transitional regime and the new Annex III date also requires clarification, particularly regarding "significant design changes" and public-authority deployments.

## Methodology Note
This report was produced by an automated research pipeline: web search, source classification, confidence scores computed from source authority, recency and corroboration, and an automated review against the extracted claims.

source_links.notes: Every link points to a gathered source.

citation_coverage.notes: Nearly all factual statements carry markdown citations consistent with the extracted claims; narrative summary sentences (e.g., 'Some sources not reflecting this amendment still cite 2 August 2026, which should be treated as outdated.') lack inline citations but are clearly derivative of claims already cited elsewhere in the body, so this is a minor stylistic issue rather than a coverage failure.

hallucination_check.notes: All dates, article numbers, and events (1 Aug 2024 entry into force, 2 Aug 2026 original date, Nov 2025 Digital Omnibus proposal, 7 May 2026 agreement, 27 July 2026 consolidated text, 2 Dec 2027 new Annex III date, 2 Aug 2028 Annex I date, Article 111(2), Article 50(2), 2 Dec 2026 marking transition) trace directly to specific extracted claims. The phrase 'including obligations for Annex III high-risk systems' attached to the high-confidence claim_001 citation slightly blends it with the separately-and-correctly-labeled low-confidence claim_002, but since the underlying fact is corroborated by claim_002's own sources (Goodwin Law), this is not a fabrication.

contradiction_disclosure.notes: The dedicated 'Contradictions & Uncertainties' section discloses the 2 Aug 2026 vs 2 Dec 2027 Annex III dispute, the European Parliament's 36-month vs 24-month discrepancy, and the Annex I 36-month vs 2 Aug 2028 discrepancy, matching all four items in the known contradictions list (the first two known contradictions are merged into one paragraph, which is acceptable).

confidence_assessment.notes: Confidence labels throughout the report align with the extracted claims' stated confidence levels (e.g., claim_002's low confidence is correctly reflected as 'low confidence' rather than being inflated alongside claim_001's high confidence; claim_005's medium confidence, claim_009's medium confidence rendered as 'low-to-medium,' and claim_010/011's low confidence are all appropriately represented).

executive_summary_accuracy.notes: The executive summary's claims (original 2 Aug 2026 date, Digital Omnibus proposal, 7 May 2026 agreement, revised 2 Dec 2027 date, and flagging of outdated sources) are all elaborated upon and supported in the body sections without contradiction.

knowledge_gaps.notes: The 'Knowledge Gaps' section addresses most open issues (formal Official Journal publication status, conditions for further date shifts, Article 111 interaction with the new Annex III date) though it omits explicit discussion of the 24-month vs 36-month timeline discrepancy noted in the open issues list; this is a minor omission rather than a failure, since that discrepancy is still disclosed in the Contradictions section.
